# Results — Study 689 (Upside Gap Two Crows)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a
bullish candle, then a black candle that gaps up away from it, then a second black
candle that engulfs the first but fails to fully close the gap, marks a top; short it**
— tested as a clean signed-**short** event study on a fixed **30-name liquid US
large-cap + SPY** basket. For every confirming bar we enter the next open (one lag),
hold 1 / 5 / 10 days short, and measure the signed return against the **unconditional**
basket base rate (not against zero — see the note below) and against a coin-flip
placebo. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; 2026-07
is dropped as partial). Fingerprint `b1038f477d11` (quantlab `data_stamp` on the 30-name
close panel) / `67c54c8a3aa2` (basket sha1, `data.fingerprint`).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLCV, `auto_adjust=True` — 30 long-listed liquid US large-caps + **SPY** (public, no key) |
| As-of | **2026-06-30** (last complete calendar month; run 2026-07-10) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-30 (**21.5** years; **162,180** total bars, 5,406 rows/name) |
| Fingerprints | `b1038f477d11` (quantlab `data_stamp`, 30-name close panel) / `67c54c8a3aa2` (`data.fingerprint`, sha1 of the same closes) |
| Detector | precise real-body upside-gap-two-crows on bars (t−2, t−1, t): bullish body, black body gapping up (body-level gap, default), second black body engulfing the first from above but not fully closing the gap; strict full-range-gap + prior-uptrend variants for the myth-check |
| Timing / costs | confirm at close of t; enter the **next open** (one lag); hold 1/5/10 days **short**; **5 / 10 bps** one-way × 2 (round trip) + **50 bps/yr** borrow on the short over the hold |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis — and it cuts the *right* way).** The basket
> is 30 names that are *still trading* in 2026. A fixed surviving-names panel
> **excludes the firms that actually topped out and crashed and delisted** — exactly
> the cases an "upside gap two crows → top" believer would point to. So this universe
> is biased **toward** finding a working bearish signal. It still finds none, which
> makes the null verdict strong rather than an artefact of selection.

## The certifying comparison — why Welch-vs-base, not a plain t-vs-zero

The basket carries the market's ordinary positive drift (equities go up on average), so
a naive one-sample *t* of the signed-**short** return against **zero** is contaminated:
it would flag "significance" merely from shorting into an up-trending tape, with or
without any upside-gap-two-crows. The fair test compares the event sample against the
**same basket's own unconditional forward-return pool** (Welch *t*) — beating "just
shorting blindly" is the bar an actual pattern-based edge has to clear. Both numbers are
reported below; **Welch *t* vs the unconditional base is the decisive number for the
Signal axis.**

## The headline — signed-SHORT forward return after an upside gap two crows

| horizon | n events | signed-short mean | unconditional base | hit-rate (Wilson 95%) | base hit-rate | Welch *t* (decisive) | HAC *t* (vs 0, informational) | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 239 | **+0.013%** | +0.028% | 46% [39.8%, 52.4%] | 48% | **+0.55** | +0.18 | 0.435 |
| 5-day  | 239 | **−0.151%** | +0.252% | 46% [39.8%, 52.4%] | 45% | **+0.52** | −0.86 | 0.738 |
| 10-day | 239 | **−0.532%** | +0.529% | 44% [37.8%, 50.3%] | 43% | **−0.01** | −1.65 | 0.951 |

Read it carefully. The signed-short mean turns **negative** at 5- and 10-day — shorting
the pattern loses at longer holds — but once compared *fairly* to the basket's own
unconditional drift (Welch *t*), **no horizon clears |t| ≥ 2**: +0.55, +0.52, −0.01.
There is no consistent directional edge either way: hit rates sit close to the
unconditional base hit rate (44% vs 43% at 10-day). The coin-flip placebo *p* runs
0.44–0.95 — the observed signed-short mean sits squarely inside the territory where a
large share of random, undirected picks would have matched or beaten it. There is no
bearish edge.

## Cost sweep — the loss only deepens

Each event is a fresh short round trip: **5 / 10 bps one-way × 2** plus **50 bps/yr**
borrow over the hold. When the gross is already flat-to-negative, costs bury it.

| horizon | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | +0.013% | **−0.089%** | −0.189% |
| 5-day  | −0.151% | **−0.261%** | −0.361% |
| 10-day | −0.532% | **−0.652%** | −0.752% |

There is no horizon where the short clears zero, let alone its costs, let alone the
unconditional base it should be beating. Nothing under the signal to charge costs
against — a textbook **Mirage**.

## Bonferroni across the basket — no single name carries it either

Per-ticker Welch *t* (event sample vs that ticker's **own** unconditional
forward-return pool — drift-neutral) at the 5-day horizon, for the 26 tickers with
≥ 6 events. With **k = 26** simultaneous tests the two-sided Bonferroni bar is
**|t| ≥ 3.10** (vs the usual 1.96):

| ticker | n | signed-short mean | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| XOM  | 10 | −1.573% | −2.01 |
| ORCL | 11 | +1.353% | +1.75 |
| INTC |  7 | +1.997% | +1.58 |

**0 / 26 tickers clear the corrected bar.** Even the most extreme name in the basket
(XOM, and note it's the *wrong* sign for a "the top is in, everything falls" story —
the other two loudest names actually point *bullish*) doesn't survive the
multiple-testing correction. No single name is quietly carrying the whole pattern —
and the signs don't even agree with each other.

## Myth check #1 — the strict true-range gap

Tighten the rule to the purist's gap (bar1's entire wick range clears bar0's high —
`true_range_gap=True`, no overlap at all, not even in the wicks). If the lore hid in a
"cleaner" gap, this should be *more* bearish. It isn't (and the events are rarer):

| horizon | n | signed-short mean | Welch *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net (5 bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 66 | +0.077% | +0.83 | +0.56 | 0.321 | −0.025% |
| 5-day  | 66 | −0.215% | +0.12 | −0.67 | 0.699 | −0.325% |
| 10-day | 66 | −0.873% | −0.65 | −1.70 | 0.922 | −0.993% |

## Myth check #2 — only patterns after a genuine prior uptrend (a true reversal)

An upside gap two crows is *supposed* to reverse a rally. Restrict to patterns that
followed a genuine prior uptrend (close at t−3 above its level 10 days earlier). Still
nothing — the Welch *t* against the unconditional base stays inside the noise band:

| horizon | n | signed-short mean | Welch *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net (5 bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 136 | −0.009% | +0.17 | −0.09 | 0.528 | −0.111% |
| 5-day  | 136 | −0.169% | +0.36 | −0.90 | 0.698 | −0.279% |
| 10-day | 136 | −0.352% | +0.43 | −0.92 | 0.786 | −0.472% |

Neither the strict full-range gap nor the prior-uptrend filter produces a certifiable
bearish edge. The pattern's predictive content is indistinguishable from the basket's
own drift under every reasonable definition.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

Deterministic OHLCV panel with an overnight-gap component and a mild embedded up-drift
(so the raw material for the pattern — an occasional bullish bar followed by two down
bars, with a real gap between them — actually occurs), with a TUNABLE planted
post-pattern crash; no network. The certifying statistic is Welch *t* vs the
unconditional base (the same drift-neutral comparison used on the real tape).

| world | Welch *t* (decisive) | HAC *t* (vs 0) | placebo *p* | hit-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.09** (sd 1.28), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 2/20 seeds** | — | — | — |
| null (edge = 0, seed 689) | −1.43 | −2.59 | 0.978 | 39% |
| planted edge = +0.012/day (seed 689) | **+2.38** | +1.85 | 0.068 | 56% |
| planted edge = +0.020/day (seed 689) | **+4.94** | +4.78 | 0.000 | 63% |

The null fires in 2 of 20 independent seeds at the 2-sigma bar — close to (and not far
above) the ~5% nominal false-positive rate of a two-sided two-sigma test, not a
systematic bias — and a planted crash of 1.2%/day or 2.0%/day lights the detector up
cleanly (*t* = 2.4 and 4.9). The harness *would* catch a real upside-gap-two-crows crash
if one existed, so the real-tape's failure to certify is a genuine **absence** of
signal, not a broken detector. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in
support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The certifying, drift-neutral comparison (Welch *t* vs the
  unconditional base) never reaches **|t| ≥ 2** at any horizon (+0.55 / +0.52 / −0.01
  for 1/5/10 days). Hit rates track the unconditional base rate. The coin-flip placebo
  places the observed mean where 44–95% of random draws would have matched or beaten
  it. **0 of 26 tickers** survive a Bonferroni correction individually — and the two
  loudest survivors point in *opposite* directions. Neither a strict full-range gap
  nor a genuine prior-uptrend filter rescues it. Carries an explicit **survivorship**
  caveat that tilts the test *toward* the claim — and it still fails. NONE, not WEAK.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The short is flat-to-negative **gross** and negative net of
  a round-trip cost + short borrow at every horizon (−0.089% to −0.652% across the 5-bps
  sweep). There is no edge to charge costs against.
- **"Marks a top"? — BUSTED.** The claim that an unfilled upside gap, dug into by two
  black crows, marks the top of a rally does not survive contact with 21.5 years of
  tape, once measured fairly against what the same basket does on an average day.
  Neither the strict gap nor the prior-uptrend filter saves it, and no individual name
  in the basket carries a Bonferroni-robust version of the story.
